task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 IDIOM/DESIGN-INTEGRITY GATE for ISS-0440. SECURITY-REVIEWER has PASSED (step-03b): out of INV-1..INV-9 scope, FAIL-refusal independently re-derived, six adjacent cases probed (missing key, null, number, list/object, legal-but-wrong, malformed JSON) all safe, mass-rewrite surface judged acceptable with the residual gap named, CI path re-verified unchanged. Do not re-run the security scope test. Review for YOUR scope: idiomatic Elixir/Mix usage, scope creep, and decision-record consistency.

1. MIX TASK IDIOM. The change adds --dir and --autofix flag parsing to run/1, plus resolve_dir/1, guard_empty_scope/2, @autofix_map, run_autofix/1 and autofix_file/1. Judge as Mix task code: is the argument parsing idiomatic (OptionParser vs hand-rolled -- and if OptionParser, are strict:/aliases: used appropriately so an unknown flag is an error rather than silently ignored)? Is Mix.raise the right failure mechanism for guard_empty_scope/2, consistent with how this task's existing hard-violation path exits? Is the file-rewrite implementation sound -- how is the JSON re-encoded, and does a rewrite preserve key order, formatting and trailing newline, or does it reformat the whole file? THAT LAST POINT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL: if autofix reformats a handoff wholesale rather than changing one field, its diff becomes unreviewable, which would defeat the per-file-visibility property SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS partly rests on. Check it concretely.

2. THE UNPLANNED CHANGE. The implementer threaded `dir` into check_registry_coverage/2, which the design did not specify, reportedly so H5 does not compute nonsense run_ids against a --dir fixture. SECURITY-REVIEWER confirmed it is a no-op on the default path and feeds only report-only H5 output. Judge it as SCOPE: is it a justified, minimal consequence of adding --dir (the kind of thing a design legitimately leaves to implementation), or is it scope creep that should have gone back to CODE-DESIGNER? Either verdict is fine if reasoned.

3. DOCS CHANGE. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3 gained Mechanism B's procedural clause. Verify it reads as an inseparable part of the existing dispatch procedure rather than a bolt-on step that could be skipped independently -- that positioning is the entire basis of Mechanism B's claimed value. Also verify it does NOT overclaim: after three design rework cycles specifically about overclaiming, the protocol text must not assert structural enforcement it does not have. The design's settled position is that Mechanism B is procedural (1.3's reliability class) and that detection is guaranteed only once the linter executes.

4. NO REINTRODUCED OVERCLAIM IN CODE. Check every new @moduledoc line, comment and user-facing output string in lint_handoffs.ex for unqualified enforcement claims. The banner and the refusal message are user-facing and will be read by future agents; they must not assert more than the design allows. This is the fourth checkpoint for this specific defect class in this run -- it has appeared at a different layer each time.

5. SCOPE CREEP GENERALLY. Confirm nothing else rode along: no change to @legal_statuses, the grandfathering lists, H1-H6's existing verdicts, or any other check's behaviour. `git diff main...HEAD --stat` is your starting point.

6. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY. Check against docs/migration/decisions/ -- particularly 0004-humanless-pipeline.md, since this change touches the enforcement model that decision record describes, and ISS-0441 (filed this run) documents that the model's gates are procedurally rather than structurally enforced. Confirm nothing here silently re-decides that.

You may READ anything. Do not edit lib/ or test/. Do NOT run --autofix against the real handoffs/ corpus -- scratch directory outside the repo only. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL and per-item verdicts; on PASS route to TEST-DESIGNER. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.
